title: TargetGroupBinding gains multiClusterTargetGroup — apply the CRDs by hand under Helm

detection.reason: reads the installed CRD's top-level spec field names (crdSpecFields[], agent 0.4.154+); TargetGroupBinding multiClusterTargetGroup is v2.10.0's addition — an older agent writes no field list, which reads not projected, never clean

quote: 🚨 🚨 🚨 We’ve added the multiClusterTargetGroup field to the TargetGroupBinding which users can set in order to share target groups among different Kubernetes clusters. Make sure to update the CRD definition in your cluster. If you're upgrading the charts using helm upgrade, you need to update CRDs manually: `kubectl apply -k "github.com/aws/eks-charts/stable/aws-load-balancer-controller/crds?ref=master"`
remediation: Run kubectl apply -k "github.com/aws/eks-charts/stable/aws-load-balancer-controller/crds?ref=master" before upgrading when installed with helm. A binding that sets multiClusterTargetGroup: true on the old schema loses the field and the controller deregisters the other cluster's targets.
verifyCommand: kubectl get crd targetgroupbindings.elbv2.k8s.aws -o json | jq -r '[.spec.versions[] | select(.served) | .name] as $v | (.spec.versions[] | select(.storage) | .schema.openAPIV3Schema.properties.spec.properties // {} | keys) as $k | "served=\($v | join(",")) spec fields=\($k | join(","))"'  # the installed CRD schema; multiClusterTargetGroup absent from the field list means the CRDs were not re-applied for this release

title: Reference IAM policy gains ec2:GetSecurityGroupsForVpc — update the controller's policy

detection.reason: IAM lives in AWS; the hint names the controller Deployment whose role to simulate

quote: ELB has updated their managed policy to include `ec2:GetSecurityGroupsForVpc`. We have updated the Load Balancer Controller policy to reflect that change. Please be sure to apply the latest IAM policy when upgrading.
remediation: Apply the v2.10.0 reference IAM policy at your convenience: the line mirrors the AWS-managed ELB policy, the controller itself does not call ec2:GetSecurityGroupsForVpc on any release (nothing fails without it).
verifyCommand: SA=$(kubectl get deploy -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.template.spec.containers[]?.image? // "" | test("aws-load-balancer-controller")) | "\(.metadata.namespace) \(.spec.template.spec.serviceAccountName)"' | head -1); ROLE=$(kubectl get sa -n ${SA% *} ${SA##* } -o jsonpath='{.metadata.annotations.eks\.amazonaws\.com/role-arn}'); aws iam simulate-principal-policy --policy-source-arn "$ROLE" --action-names ec2:GetSecurityGroupsForVpc --query 'EvaluationResults[].[EvalActionName,EvalDecision]' --output text  # every row must read allowed; implicitDeny means the controller's IAM policy predates this release (Pod Identity: read the association's role with aws eks list-pod-identity-associations --cluster-name ... --namespace ... --service-account ...)
coversNotes: v2.10.0 (Enhancement and Fixes): Add new ec2:GetSecurityGroupsForVpc permission to LBC policy.
